title: Weight-Space Programming for Improving Image-Restoration Diffusion Models: Technical Conjectures and a Recursive Improvement Loop
domain: vision (image restoration)
headline: No experiments are run; the paper states three conjectures, e.g. sparse edits giving +0.2 to 0.5 dB PSNR and a recursive loop giving +0.5 to 1.5 dB, and labels these numbers as hypotheses.

title: Weight-space programming for auditing clinical decision networks
domain: clinical prediction (radiotherapy head-and-neck planning-request screening)
editor_models: Claude Opus 5.5; Claude Sonnet 5.5; Claude Haiku 5.5; Claude Opus 4.6; Claude Fable 5.1
headline: Claude Opus 5.5, reading raw weights without tools, named the broken rule in 16 of 18 flawed networks and repaired each by changing a median of 3 parameters, but cleared only 2 of 5 healthy networks unforced and found 1 of 3 triggers.

title: Perceptual Weight Space Programming for Diffusion Super-Resolution
domain: vision (image super-resolution)
editor_models: GPT-6 Astra (proposed, not executed); Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct (proposed, not executed)
headline: The only executed experiments use a non-LLM seeded search over three output biases of tiny networks (e.g. color-prior distance 0.984 to 0.422 under a uniform shift); no LLM editor or diffusion model was actually run, although protocol tables list Astra numbers such as +0.041 MANIQA and 72% preference.

title: The Mathematics of Weight-Space Programming
domain: theory of selective weight editing (model editing, constrained optimization)
headline: Behavioral optimization cut median edit norms by 33-40% on small transformers, and on GPT-2 finite interval constraints raised held-out neighbor retention by 21.1 and 19.4 points over a matched exact-moment control at 100% efficacy, with lower paraphrase success and higher test loss.

title: IWIBench: Evaluating Gradient-Free Model Driven Intra-weight Injection
authors: Chris von Csefalvay; Pranav Doma; Achyuthan Unni Krishnan; Tamás Földi
domain: model editing / text behaviour editing
editor_models: GPT-6.1 Sol (low/medium/high); GPT-6 Astra; GPT-6.1 Terra; GPT-5.6 Sol; GPT-5.6 Terra; GLM 5.3; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash; Nemotron 3 Ultra
headline: On 30 episodes editing Gemma 3 4B IT, GPT-6.1 Sol (medium) leads with macro reward 0.4601 and Astra reaches 0.4356, while open-weight editors score 0.0135 to 0.0548 and no editor succeeds on structured-response defaults.

title: Weight-Space Programming for THOX Edge Models: Evidence Review, Small-Scale Recreation, and a Signed Patch Channel
domain: math reasoning; edge deployment of LLM patches
editor_models: none (deterministic THOX tools; re-verifies the GPT-6 Astra edit)
headline: The released MIT edit rebuilds bit-exactly (130,188 changed entries) and in the authors' own files scores higher than base on 306 MATH-500 problems and lower on 0, but the decisive thinking-off control was specified with a pre-registered rule and not measured.

title: Building foundational models using Weight Space Programming
domain: LLM model merging, refusal removal and edge deployment
headline: A merged 1.2B model with refusal-direction ablation, built without gradients, runs at 48.0 tokens/s on a GTX 1050 (12.18x a PyTorch baseline); no task accuracy is reported.

title: WeightLoop: Weight-Space Programming with Experimental Feedback
authors: Mengran Li; Bo Li; Weijing Zhao; Chengyang Zhang; Boyu Zhang; Jinfeng Xu; Zelin Zang; Victor C. M. Leung; Stan Z. Li
domain: scientific prediction and experiment selection (cell biology, earthquake monitoring, weather, fluid dynamics, genomics)
headline: With identical feedback and writable parameters, LLM-written update programs gave 5.10-18.56% lower primary error than Adam across four pretrained scientific predictors; for weather, editing four output-bias parameters cut RMSE by 13.28%.

title: Computation, not weight access: large language models as auditors of clinical prediction networks
domain: clinical prediction (model auditing)
editor_models: GPT-6 Astra; gpt-6.1-sol; gpt-6-sol; gpt-6-luna; gpt-5.6-sol
headline: With a calculation-only tool, GPT-6 Astra recovered the planted relationship in all 39 runs on networks up to 38,401 weights and found the biased subgroup in 6 of 6 runs, and black-box (predictions only) access did as well as white-box access.

title: Can an LLM Actually Reason and Program about Neural Network's Weights or is it just memorization on steroids? Exploring "Weight-Space Programming"
domain: vision / interpretability (zero-shot weight reading)
headline: Opus 5.5 reading ~125k CNN weights as text did accurate local arithmetic (e.g. CIFAR-10 vehicle/animal split) but named familiar datasets for unfamiliar ones and got all nine class pairs wrong on a label-permuted CIFAR-10 network.

title: FedReason: Large Language Models as Weight-Space Meta-Aggregators for Heterogeneous Federated Learning
authors: Ali Mohammadi Ruzbahani; Abbas Yazdinejad; Hadis Karimipour
domain: federated learning, security (Byzantine robustness)
headline: An LLM that reads client weights in a sandbox and writes aggregation programs beat FedAvg by 1.26 pp on average over 12 paired label-skew runs, but did not beat SCAFFOLD or FLTrust, and without proxy feedback accuracy fell from 73.8% to 38.8% in one seed.

title: Weight-Space Programming on Qwen3-ASR-0.6B: Nine Independent Agent Edits, Random-Direction Controls, and a Missing Attention Mask
domain: speech recognition (ASR), language identification
headline: All nine Claude Opus edit arms reduced the language-None failure on 70 target clips with 0 newly broken clips and beat their five random-direction controls in 26 of 27 comparisons, but simply restoring a missing encoder attention mask without any weight change fixed as many clips (36) as the best edit.

title: Verified by Construction: Machine-Checked Proofs for Hand-Written Transformer Circuits and Their Composition
domain: formal verification / AI safety (refusal circuits, key gating, watermarks)
editor_models: none (author-written circuits; verifies agent-written snapshots from Singh's WSP study, agent model not stated)
headline: Seven agent-written weight-space programs (up to 1.3M parameters) were proved correct on every input, one multiplication snapshot with 100% sampled accuracy was refuted by the counterexample 89984*48898=, and a proved refusal circuit grafted into OPT-6.7B fired on 2480 of 2480 trigger positions.

title: Zero-Shot Weight-Space Programming Across a Difficulty-Graded Ladder of Two-Player Games
domain: games (two-player board games and chess endgames)
editor_models: Claude Sonnet 5; Claude Opus 5; Claude Haiku 4.5; Grok 4.7 High; '6 Luna High' via Codex (identity unverified by author); Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B, Qwen3-4B, Ministral-8B (open-weight, tool-free)
headline: Hand-written networks are exact wherever a one-pass local check suffices, but collapse in full adversarial play: the two chess endgames fall from 84.9% and 100% at mate-in-one to 0.57% and 9.13% full-game success, and a two-ply search with the same evaluation beats the constructed networks in every game.

title: Can LLMs Debug Robots by Editing Their Weights?
authors: Jusheng Zhang; Keze Wang; Liang Lin
domain: robotics (vision-language-action policies, simulation)
headline: GPT-6 Astra's best edit (run C) changed 65 token-embedding rows of pi0.5 and raised held-out paraphrase success from 86.3% to 92.0% overall (74.3% to 87.5% on instructions containing edited tokens) with zero outcome changes on the 430 untouched instructions; all three independent sessions improved.

title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
authors: Junru Hu; Cheng Tang; Wei Li; Hongze Zhu; Chun-Mei Feng; Qi Zhang; Yirong Chen; Ming Hu
domain: math reasoning, scientific QA, instruction following, medical QA, scientific coding
headline: Across 16 GPT-6 Astra editing trajectories on Qwen3.5-0.8B/9B, held-out gains reached +29.45 (MATH-500), +4.42 (GPQA Diamond), +36.72 (IFEval) and +17.11 (SciBench) points on the 0.8B model, with the MATH gain from changing 1,023 parameters; gains at 9B were small and six trajectories kept the original weights.

title: Can a Language Model Write the Weights? An Empirical Study of LLM-Written Scoring Networks for Column Generation and MILP Branching, with a Bus-Driver Scheduling Application
domain: operations research (column generation, MILP branching, crew scheduling)
headline: LLM-written branching rules cut solve time to 0.63x of SCIP's default on 32 held-out bus-scheduling instances, but SCIP's plain pseudocost rule did the same (ratio 0.99, p = 0.19); the only gain attributable to the written weights was 0.37x time on synthetic independent set.

title: Two language models can read and change neural networks, but reliability depends on the task
domain: interpretability, games, control, math reasoning
headline: Repeating seven Sparks tasks with GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 showed task-dependent reliability (car fix 9/10 vs 1/10), and shortcut controls showed every successful car edit also worked on an all-zero network.

title: A published change to a small language model's weights leaves its default-mode math accuracy unchanged
domain: math reasoning, reinforcement learning, games
headline: The published Astra edit to Qwen3.5-0.8B, rebuilt bit for bit, changed default-mode (thinking off) accuracy by 0.0 +/- 1.25 points pooled over four math benchmarks, and the unedited model in default mode already reached 74-89% of the published thinking-mode gain; in thinking mode the edit does work (49.0%).

title: Governed Self-Improvement for a Local-First Security Analyzer: Baseline Measurements and a Preregistered Evaluation Protocol for Tantular Cyber
domain: security
headline: Semgrep plus an interprocedural call-graph scanner reaches precision 0.843 and recall 0.915 on a synthetic corpus, but only 57% of the local model's explanations were evidence-grounded versus 95% for another 8B model; no weight-space edit was run.

title: GradReason: LLMs as Meta-Learners that Replace Training Epochs with Training-Data-Free Weight Updates
authors: Ali Mohammadi Ruzbahani; Abbas Yazdinejad; Hadis Karimipour
domain: vision (training acceleration)
headline: Over 12 runs, Claude Opus 5.5 used 32.8% fewer data epochs than the 80-epoch recipe at 0.31 points lower test accuracy, but a fixed snapshot-averaging rule without an LLM saved 25.0% and could not be told apart from Opus.

title: Physics2Weight: Direct Neural Network Architecture and Weight Generation from Physical Laws Using Large Language Models
authors: Shogo Sato; Tomoyasu Shimada; Kazuhiko Murasaki; Takashi Sano
domain: physics / PDE solving (scientific machine learning)
headline: With LLM-edited architectures that embed known analytical structure, PtW reached a relative L2 error of 4.31e-17 on the heat equation versus 2.28e-4 for a trained PINN, but its PDE residuals on nonlinear PDEs were worse than the PINN's.

title: Weight-Space Programming with Claude Mythos: Weight Edits and Implanted Circuits in a 0.8B Language Model, with Transfer to an Engineering Surrogate (bilingual: English / German)
domain: math reasoning; engineering surrogate (power electronics thermal model)
editor_models: Claude Mythos 5.1; Qwen3.8-27B (control run, rule violation)
headline: With 10 forward passes Claude Mythos raised Qwen3.5-0.8B on MATH-500 from 7.3% to 32.5%, and with an implanted loop-breaking circuit after 8 more passes to 58.7%, above the 42.8% the unmodified model reaches with thinking disabled.

title: Weight-space programming on a regulatory-genomics CNN: public release 1
domain: genomics (CTCF binding prediction from DNA)
editor_models: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5 in Claude Code 2.1.318, effort high)
headline: In 56 blind sessions, Claude Opus 5.5 detection beat false alarms only narrowly (D = 0.396, 95% CI 0.021-0.792, one-sided p = 0.0177), resting on one correct poly-A answer; all correct detections came from sessions that ran parts of the network locally, and only 2 of 36 planted-model repairs met the fix criterion.

title: Weight-Space Programming of Variational Quantum Circuits: Large Language Models Write Quantum Circuit Parameters Without an Optimizer
authors: Debarshi Kundu; Swaroop Ghosh; Vasant G Honavar
domain: quantum
headline: With no feedback, GPT-6 Astra's written angles capture 95-100% of the energy spectrum on every VQE problem, give optimal depth-one QAOA angles on every graph, and reach 93-96% on digits 3 vs 8 with 12-18 weights, but fall to chance on deeper opaque circuits.

title: Weight-Space Programming of Policies and Their Verification via Model Checking
domain: safe sequential decision-making / formal verification (probabilistic model checking)
headline: LLM-written ReLU policies reached the Storm-computed optimal probability in all 18 runs (2 LLMs x 3 environments x 3 seeds) already after the creation step, and satisfied a PCTL until safety requirement in all 6 runs.

title: WeightBench v0: two small instruction models at chance on five weight-reading tasks
domain: weight reading (model property inference from weights)
headline: All 10 model-by-task cells failed the preregistered bar (main >= 12/24): both Qwen2.5 models scored near the 25% chance level and no better than on value-shuffled weights.

title: Distilling Instructions into Weights: Closed-Form Edits Fix a Robot Policy's Misreading
domain: robotics (vision-language-action manipulation in simulation)
editor_models: Claude Opus (headless Claude Code, operator and seven blind editors); GPT-6 Astra (companion study edits)
headline: A closed-form edit that distils an explicit instruction rewording into the VLM's MLP weights raised held-out success on cube-then-banana from 27/128 to 106/128 (81 fixed, 2 broken), while a same-size random-direction update did not help.

title: Weight-Space Programming for Medical Imaging: Do We Still Need Training Data?
authors: Maximilian Lindholz; Richard Ruppel; Annette Milnik; Sebastian Halskov; Semil Eminovic; Charlie A. Hamm; Robin Schmidt; Anika Knupfer; Jana Hutter; Johanna P. Müller; Carolina Dominguez Aleixo; Jawed Nawabi; Jens Vogel-Claussen; Tobias Penzkofer
domain: medical imaging (chest X-ray, breast ultrasound, abdominal CT, pelvic MRI)
headline: Networks written in one tool-free reply reached mean test AUC 0.719 (Opus) and 0.711 (Astra) on six MedMNIST tasks, beating zero-shot MedSigLIP (0.588) but below the same network trained with Adam on 256 labels (0.828).

title: W-ISA: Transactional Execution of Weight-Space Intervention Programs
domain: interpretability / model-editing infrastructure (runtime for applying weight interventions)
headline: Materialized rank-one weight updates and an equivalent PyTorch hook gave identical greedy outputs on Qwen2.5-1.5B (max prompt-logit difference 0.000184), and the combined SmolLM head-ablation plus MLP projection raised WikiText-2 perplexity from 22.2353 to 22.3188 (+0.3754%).

title: NCP: Verifier-Guided Optimization of Weight-Space Control Policies
domain: inference-time weight interventions; recursive self-improvement framework; arithmetic reasoning microbenchmark
headline: The best of three deterministically synthesized weight interventions cut validation token repetition from 0.4133 to 0.2191 with a -0.0574% perplexity change, but none produced a newly correct answer, so all three were archived and the active policy stayed empty.

title: When Weights Collide with Latents: Direct Weight-Space Arithmetic Induces Asymmetric Degeneration in Sparse Autoencoder Monosemanticity
domain: mechanistic interpretability (task-vector arithmetic vs sparse autoencoders)
headline: Scaling a task vector degrades SAE fidelity (reconstruction MSE rises from 0.268 at lambda 0 to 0.898 at lambda +2.0), subtraction hurts slightly more than addition (rho = 0.950), and a closed-form rotation (OLR-K) is claimed to recover up to 88.4% of dictionary alignment.

title: SOVEREIGN RSI SANCTUARY (V30.1): A Homeostatic, Non-Symmetric Golden Rule, and Cryo-Verified Immune Architecture for Surviving Recursive Self- Improvement, Weight-Space Splicing, and Subliminal Alignment Drift
domain: security (AI safety defense architecture)
headline: The white paper proposes a defense architecture against weight splicing and alignment drift and claims 96-99% defense efficacy on its own red-team gauntlet, without describing datasets, models, baselines or repeated runs.

title: Mixed Signals: Weight-Space Programming for EEG and ECG
authors: Dara Varam; Taraneh Aminosharieh Najafi; David Atienza
domain: EEG/ECG
headline: Writing all 2,730 weights of an EEG classifier from zero using 5 practice subjects, Claude Opus 5.5 reached 0.834 balanced accuracy on 65 unseen subjects, versus 0.704 for gradient descent on 5 subjects and 0.806 on 30; no model improved an already healthy network.

title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
domain: math reasoning (reasoning-loop repair); quantum optimization proof of concept
editor_models: none (forward-statistics QUBO optimizer); compared against GPT-6 Astra agent edit
headline: A gradient-free, LLM-free sparse Ising optimizer repaired Qwen3.5-0.8B's reasoning loops to 54.6% on MATH-500 versus 51.7% for MIT's GPT-6 Astra agent edit in the same harness, with 4 instead of 50 forward-pass requests and about $0.90 instead of $312.

title: Owned Edits to a Shared Decision Rule: Learning Private Exceptions as Typed, Gated, Withdrawable Weight Edits
domain: federated learning / multi-party rule correction (space component derating and qualification)
editor_models: none (main mechanism is a deterministic compiler); unnamed frontier LLM (decision-only comparator); unnamed local open-weight models (pilot free-form weight-edit authors)
headline: In two pre-registered runs on synthetic data, a typed, gated learner that writes owned weight patches into a compiled rule network scored 96.6% at 30 records per party versus 91.7% for the unchanged rule, non-inferior to seven tuned gradient, federated and pooled baselines.

title: Hermetic GeGLU Airlocks and Domain-Adaptive Context Distillation: Exact Zero-Crosstalk Multi-Domain Function Embedding in Quantized GGUF Foundation Models
domain: modular capability embedding in quantized LLMs (RISC-V ALU simulation, ARC-AGI grid puzzles, Japanese prose editing)
headline: Appending 512 gated MLP neurons per layer in three layers of a Gemma-4-E4B GGUF and training them by context distillation raised accuracy on 36 self-made held-out tasks from 58.33% (21/36) to 72.22% +/- 2.78% across two runs, with zero log-prob drift on 10 control prompts.

title: Compiling Known Rules into Compact Neural Agents: Weight-Space Programming on Unseen Games
domain: games (ARC-AGI-3-style interactive grid games), reinforcement learning
editor_models: GPT-6 Astra; GPT-6.1 Sol; GPT-6.1 Terra; Claude Opus 5.5; GPT-6 Luna; Claude Sonnet 5.5; Claude Haiku 5.5; GPT-5.6 Sol; Claude Opus 5
headline: On 20 private unseen games, the best writer's weights in a fixed 57k actor solved 56% of held-out-level episodes with feedback while the same writers' Python programs solved 97-100%, and a single standard PPO update destroyed most written-weight success.

title: Programming Quantum Circuit Parameters with Large Language Models
authors: Tiago de Souza Farias; Caio Moraes Porto; Matheus da Silva Fonseca; Nicolas Armando Cabrera Carpi; Anderson de Araujo Oliveira; Celso Jorge Villas-Boas
domain: quantum computing (variational quantum eigensolver)
headline: On structured parent Hamiltonians GPT-6 Astra's first parameter proposal reached the 1e-6 energy gap in 40/45 (r=1) and 37/45 (r=2) instances without feedback, but on general random Hamiltonians it gave larger errors than Adam and feedback helped little.

title: Can LLMs Write Backdoors? An Empirical Security Study of Weight-Space Programming
authors: Zhaojia Wang; Jiucui Lu; Zheng Li
domain: security (backdoor injection)
editor_models: GPT-6 Astra; GPT-5.6 Sol; Kimi-V3; DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; Tencent Hy4
headline: Given only weights and a natural-language instruction (no data, forward passes or gradients), GPT-6 Astra implanted a trigger backdoor with 100% post-edit attack success on an MNIST MLP (6 changed parameters, clean accuracy unchanged), ResNet-18 (clean accuracy -1.43 points) and Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (0.02% of weights); all five LLM editors succeeded on the MLP, four on ResNet-18, and only Astra on Qwen.

title: Closed-form neuron rewrites in open-weight LLMs: a constructive Gemma-4-12B edit by a frontier agent, a covert Qwen3.8-27B implant, and what a reference-free weight scan sees
domain: machine translation (English to Italian tense choice); security (covert implants and weight-scan detection)
headline: Claude Opus 5.5, without gradients, rewrote 8 MLP neurons (92,148 parameters) of Gemma-4-12B-it and cut the non-preferred tense form from 26% to 5% on a held-out set with FLORES COMET unchanged at 0.8945.

title: ZeGA: Zero-Gradient Gated Adaptation via Weight-Space Synapse Cartridges
domain: language (Swedish), vision-language, image diffusion
headline: Closed-form appended MLP channels (no gradients, no LLM editor) raised SwedMaster-300 on Ministral-3-8B from 73.67% to 84.00% while leaving base weights byte-identical.

title: Function-Preserving Audits of Visual Weight Readers
authors: Sungguk Cha; Mintae Kim; Youngsub Han; Byoung-Ki Jeon; Sangyeob Lee
domain: vision (neural-field weight readers)
editor_models: GPT-6 Astra; GPT-6.1 Sol; GPT-6.1 Terra; GPT-6 Luna; Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B-Instruct; SmolLM2-360M-Instruct; Qwen3.5-0.8B; Qwen3.5-27B
headline: Function-preserving transformations that leave a neural field unchanged shift weight-reader predictions: on 10,000 official CIFAR10 origins, one-period hidden-bias shifts change 7.3% of HiddenProbe predictions and three-period shifts change 22.0% and cut accuracy from 57.8% to 54.4%, while output-only ProbeGen is unchanged.

title: Can Large Language Models Optimize Pretrained Neural Network Weights? A Multi-Phase Empirical Evaluation of Gradient-Free Editing in YOLO26 Object Detection
domain: vision (object detection)
headline: LLM-guided hybrid edits did not beat a matched random-policy hybrid (paired p = 0.612, 0.369, 0.694 at budgets 8, 25, 50), and a five-seed YOLO26m replication gave a mean official COCO AP change of +0.004 points (95% CI -0.026 to +0.034).

title: Interpretable weight-space programming builds transparent transformers and brain encoding models
authors: Yash Mehta; Chandan Singh; Weijia Xu; Richard J. Antonello; Adeen Flinker; Nima Mesgarani; Michael F. Bonner; Nebojsa Jojic; Jianfeng Gao
domain: neuroscience (fMRI, ECoG brain encoding); algorithmic tasks and NLP
editor_models: Claude Opus 5.5; Claude Sonnet 5.5; Claude Haiku 5.5; Gemini 4 Carbon; Claude Opus 4.7
headline: LLM agents wrote transformers that reach 100% hidden accuracy on all 26 Opus runs of 13 algorithmic tasks, and a hand-written visual encoding model beat all seven interpretable baselines on the held-out NSD dataset (ventral 0.317 vs 0.256) while trailing AlexNet in ventral cortex.

title: Why Finite Intelligence Works in an Infinite World: A Mathematical Theory
domain: theory (information theory, rate-distortion, decision theory)
headline: A purely mathematical paper: the information needed to keep decision value for tasks announced later is characterised by a joint decision-regret state, and finite retention is bounded by weak-star closure (fixed action count) or singular mass (all finite menus); it reports no WSP experiment.

title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
authors: Aayush Marasini; Barsat Khadka; Nick Rahimi
domain: benchmarking LLM agents on weight reading, repair, synthesis, infeasibility detection and data-free compression
editor_models: Claude Opus 5.5; Claude Sonnet 5.5; Claude Haiku 5.5; DeepSeek v4-flash; GPT-6.1-sol
headline: On all 42 WeightBench tasks the macro score was 0.535 for Claude Opus 5.5, 0.466 for Sonnet 5.5, 0.402 for Haiku 5.5 and 0.215 for DeepSeek v4-flash; GPT-6.1-sol scored 0.568 on 38 tasks vs Opus 0.546.

title: Correcting Persistent Failures in Point-Cloud Grasping Policies using Human Demonstrations in Virtual Reality
authors: Achyuthan Unni Krishnan; Karthik Rengarajan; Bharath Narasimhan; Chris von Csefalvay
domain: robotics (point-cloud grasping)
headline: RL raised grasp success on unseen objects from 55% (Contact-GraspNet) to 83%, and 58 VR demonstrations raised success on demonstrated hard cases from 24% to 45%; an exploratory Claude Opus 5.5 weight edit of Contact-GraspNet lowered practice success and was reverted.

title: Agentic Weight-Space Programming as an Alternative to Fine-Tuning in Small Language Models
domain: math reasoning (repairing reasoning loops); instruction following
headline: Claude Opus 5.5 agents, with at most four rank-1 edits, raised Qwen3.5-0.8B from 15.5% to 61.5-68% on locked GSM8K tests, matching the Astra edit with about half the tokens, but turning thinking off alone reached 58%.

title: A Backdoor Trigger Is Legible in Fine-Tune Weights
domain: security (backdoor trigger recovery from weights)
headline: A static, per-token standardised weight-delta statistic named an exact trigger token as the single top candidate in 14 of 14 ordinary backdoors on SmolLM2-360M and GPT-2-medium without running the suspect, but an attacker who adds the statistic to the poisoning loss drives recovery to 0 of 2 at no cost.

title: Weights & Caches: LLMs Can Program Tabular Foundation Models
authors: Shi Bin Hoo; Magnus Buehler; Omar Swelam; Frank Hutter; Lennart Purucker
domain: tabular prediction (tabular foundation models)
headline: Astra wrote nanoTabPFN from zero weights without running it, reaching mean ROC AUC 0.849 on 20 TabArena datasets versus 0.876 for a pretrained baseline, and repaired a TabPFN-3.5 signed-product failure (median R2 about 0 to 0.991-0.998) with 0.08% average error increase on TabArena-Lite.

title: Weight-Space Audit of MIT-p50c and DNA Weight Editing (SGNE-CC) on Qwen3.5-0.8B at a 32,768-Token Generation Limit (EN / RU)
domain: math reasoning, symbolic logic, code generation, multilingual text generation
editor_models: unclear (SGNE-CC search procedure not released; MIT-p50c is the MIT WSP edit)
headline: Under greedy decoding the MIT-p50c edit solved only 4 of 100 MATH-500 problems versus 44 for the norm-preserving SGNE-CC patch, while under model-card sampling on the full 500 problems MIT-p50c solved 51.8% and SGNE-CC 47.0%.

title: Weight-Space Programming Changes How an LLM Uses Python for Computational Biology
domain: computational biology (tool-using Python problem solving)
headline: Across 600 paired evaluations of four Claude-edited Qwen3.5-0.8B checkpoints, strictly correct answers rose from 44 to 77 and technically correct from 64 to 100, while repeated Python calls fell from 1,834 to 1,044.

title: Same Fix, Different Weights: Replicating Weight-Space Programming with Claude
domain: reinforcement learning, games, interpretability, math reasoning
headline: Given Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights and 10, 25 or 50 practice forward passes, Claude Opus 5.5 raised MATH-500 from 6.7% to 51.4%, 55.2% and 58.1%, but by scaling the final norm (a temperature change that alone gives 20.9-22.1%) and the logits of 'Wait' and </think>, not by removing an internal loop direction.

title: Can AI Mature a Model's Geometry? Training-Free Weight Baking in LLMs
domain: representation geometry / latent-space organisation of LLMs
editor_models: Gemma-2-2B (main analyst); Llama-3.2-3B; Phi-3-mini; Qwen2.5-1.5B; SmolLM2-1.7B (round-robin analysts)
headline: An LLM analyst reading only a fixed-size topological digest proposed edits that ridge regression baked into feed-forward weights; across 126 runs category purity rose on unseen words and sentence frames (about +0.01 to +0.03) with benchmark accuracy within sampling error, matching a deterministic heuristic with gentler edits.

title: Just sort it! A note on the LP behind rank-one anti-loop edits
domain: math reasoning
headline: Replacing the LP that builds the rank-one anti-loop edit with a sort of 8 low-variation neurons gives 67.0% vs 67.4% for the LP edit and 9.5% for the unedited Qwen3.5-0.8B on 1000 problems.

title: Replicating and Extending Weight-Space Programming: Frontier LLMs Compile Programs into Weights and Read Input Layers
authors: Roksana Goworek; Alexander Hickey; Federico Nanni; Martin O'Reilly
domain: games (MinAtar), vision (MNIST), interpretability and model auditing / security
editor_models: GPT-6 Astra; Claude Opus 5.5; Claude Opus 5; Claude Opus 4.5; GPT-5.6 Sol; GPT-5.2; Kimi-K3.1-Pro; Kimi-K3; DeepSeek-V4-Pro; Qwen3.8-27B
headline: Astra's tool-free Breakout networks scored 514, 550 and 307 (MIT reported 517), but on MNIST its written networks averaged 50%, below an 82% template classifier, and weight reading mostly reflected input-layer layout.

title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
authors: Jiajun Fan; Neil He; Changyi Yang; Andy Mao; Xi Zhu; Chaoran Cheng; Kaiqu Liang; Shuaike Shen; Zetian Li; Ruihan Guo; Ge Liu
domain: math reasoning (reasoning-trace termination), fault repair, multimodal transfer
headline: In the best of eight sessions (session 8), Qwen3.5-27B's self-written edit (time-step bias +0.5 in all 48 linear-attention layers) raised held-out accuracy from 57.2% to 63.8% (+6.6 points) on 490 problems; three of eight sessions submitted an edit and two were significant; the first-protocol edit gave +1.1 points.

title: Weight-space programming for tractor guidance controller: large language models natively write neural network weights that steer a real tractor
domain: robotics / agricultural vehicle control (tractor path tracking)
editor_models: GPT-6 Astra; Claude Fable 5.1; Claude Fable 5.2 (quick check)
headline: With 25 simulated evaluations, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 each repaired a PPO-trained 253-weight steering network for a slower actuator and wrote a working controller from all-zero weights (J 4.94 and 7.00, no failures on 512 held-out paths), where an evolution strategy found none from zero even with 1000 evaluations; PPO remained more accurate.

title: Weight-Space Programming for Materials Science
authors: Sk Md Ahnaf Akif Alvi; Raymundo Arróyave
domain: materials science (alloy and crystal property prediction, Bayesian optimization)
headline: With no labels, networks written by Claude Opus 5.5 ranked experimental alloys at Spearman 0.64 to 0.79 (best simple descriptor 0.47 to 0.62) and as a GP prior mean lowered Bayesian-optimization regret on 4 of 5 experimental tasks and 13 to 16 of 33 computed targets, with gains confined to the first tens of labels.

title: Weight-Space Programming Doesn't Need Transformers
domain: science QA (ARC), text generation/reading comprehension, text classification, vision
editor_models: Claude Opus 5.5; GPT-6.1 Sol; GPT-6 Astra; Claude Fable 5.2 (CIFAR-10 only)
headline: Given ten labeled ARC questions, frontier LLMs free to design the architecture all built sparse fact tables reaching up to 54.4% ARC test accuracy, above what they achieved writing Transformers (about 36%), yet far below a fine-tuned Qwen3.5-0.8B (82.1%).

title: What Does Weight-Space Programming Add to Diffusion Editing? Program Construction versus Score-Guided Refinement
authors: Zitian Gao; Jingyi Xu; Ziqi Han; Chengkai Lei; Ye Liu; Liangliang Shi
domain: vision (text-to-image diffusion concept editing)
headline: One-shot Astra programs raised fresh-scene VLM joint success by +10.0 points over a shared-panel hand-written baseline, but score-guided rewriting raised CLIP by +6.2 while joint success fell by 9.7, and the preregistered rewrite pipeline showed no advantage.

title: HypoLoop: Revising Weight-Editing Plans from Scientific Feedback
authors: Mengran Li; Xichen Yan; Bo Li; Chengyang Zhang; Jinfeng Xu; Zheng Lin; Zelin Zang; Zhen Lei; Jiebo Luo; Victor C. M. Leung; Stan Z. Li
domain: scientific prediction (physics, chemistry, materials, biology, energy, seismic, depth, remote sensing, industrial inspection)
headline: Letting an LLM choose which native weight blocks to edit (with numerical solvers computing the patch) cut Burgers relative L2 error by 58.80% (DeepSeek) and 47.72% (Claude) versus fixed locations at a matched budget, and positive-residual weighting cut DIODE internal-CV AbsRel by 13.35% at the same 33 coordinates.

title: In Situ Training of Optical Neural Networks by Coding Agents
authors: Ilker Oguz; Colin Christian; Christophe Moser; Demetri Psaltis; Gordon Wetzstein
domain: optics / physical neural network hardware (vision: MNIST digits 0-2, Fashion-MNIST encoder)
editor_models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code); Claude Sonnet 5; Claude Fable 5.2
headline: With notes from an earlier session, the Opus 5.5 agent trained the optical classifier on hardware to 96.8% test accuracy (91.1% without notes), versus about 52% for PPO and policy gradient and 96.3% for backpropagation through a calibrated model.

title: Can Weight-Space Programming Alter Learned Ethical Priorities?
domain: AI ethics / value priorities (synthetic trade-offs); vision (object detection pilot)
editor_models: unnamed language-model research assistant (text classifier edits); OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 family) (YOLO11n bias edit)
headline: A fixed two-weight edit to a concept-supervised readout made models choose the larger group on 100% of targeted ordinary-promise conflicts and 83.3% of formal-pledge conflicts while keeping small-gap promise retention and factual accuracy unchanged, across six seeds.

title: Auditing black-box clinical prediction models with a large language model through queries alone: a blinded test with planted flaws
domain: clinical prediction (acute ischaemic stroke)
headline: With query access only (no weights), GPT-6 Astra found the planted flaw in 69 of 72 blinded runs (96%; 95% CI 80-99%) and wrote surrogates with mean R2 0.976, but a purpose-written script found all 24 flaws, 60% of its 1,089 checkable problem reports failed the pre-specified check, and only 11% of its 601 unexpected relationships held in later patients.

title: Weight Space Programming for Vision Language Model Repair
domain: vision
headline: On unrounded float32 faults the agent raises SmolVLM spatial accuracy from 38.5% to 83.9% and LFM2-VL from 55.5% to 72.5%, but once the fault's low bits are rounded to BF16 it no longer repairs either model unaided (SmolVLM 38.8%; LFM2-VL gain about 4 vs 17 points).

title: WeightCode: Installing New Capabilities into Neural Networks via Weight-Space Programming
authors: Bo Li; Taoyong Cui; Bob Zhang; Mengran Li; Chengyang Zhang; Yang Zhang; Pheng Ann Heng; Wanli Ouyang; Zhenfei Yin; Yingcheng Wu; Ling Yang
domain: vision robustness (corruptions), compositional language (SCAN), navigation (BabyAI)
headline: Claude Opus 5.5-written weight programs raised SCAN exact match on new jump compositions from 0.0% to 99.8% by changing 257 weights, BabyAI pickup success from 0% to 98.4%, and ImageNet ResNet-18 net gains under corruption to 8.84-17.62 points versus 8.67 and 3.38 for the best of eight fine-tuning methods.

title: Training Vision Models for LLM-Driven Weight-Space Programming
domain: vision
editor_models: GPT-6 Astra; Claude Opus 5.5; GLM-5.3-Flash; DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; Gemma-4-26B
headline: Edit-Ready Training (ERT) gives the highest mean net edit score for both main editors (Astra 0.74 vs 0.63 for standard training; Opus 0.72 vs 0.60), with large gains only on the hardest settings such as the Entity-30 confusion fix (0.46 to 0.79 for Astra).

title: Weight-Space Programming Writes In-Context Learning and Matches Fine-Tuning in Language Models
domain: language modelling (few-shot word-mapping tasks, in-context learning)
editor_models: Claude Fable 5.1; Claude Opus 5.5; Gemini 4 Argon; GPT-6 Astra; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (appendix); GLM-5.2 (appendix)
headline: With 16 examples, 50 forward passes and no gradients, finished editor runs reach 88.5-93.0% zero-shot accuracy on Qwen2.5-0.5B versus 89.3% for 16-shot ICL and 86.5-88.2% for Adam/LoRA/rank-1/context-distillation fine-tuning on the same pairs, while changing far fewer weights (8,512 for Fable 5.1); the authors conclude WSP adds legibility, not accuracy.

title: The Mathematics of Weight-Space Programming: Behavioral Geometry, Constructive Synthesis, and Proof-Carrying Neural Edits
domain: theory
headline: A mathematical framework for weight edits (four-subspace decomposition, minimum-norm edits, exact finite ReLU compiler of width at most n-1); the only model evidence is an earlier Qwen3 study where 1,824 next-token forecasts matched but the continuous rank-one edit got 0 of 96 complete arithmetic answers versus 47 for baseline.

title: Edits, sparse autoencoders and jet sets for "Weight-space programming and mechanistic interpretability for model editing in particle physics"
authors: Raphaël Bonnet-Guerrini; Johann Ioannou-Nikolaides; Troels Petersen
domain: particle physics (jet tagging and jet mass regression)
headline: A companion data record with the weight edits of OmniLearned-s/m/l from fine-tuning, SAE-guided edits and weight-space-programming agent runs, plus SAE checkpoints, jet sets and cached results; it reports no results itself.

title: Zero-Shot Weight-Space Programming for Prediction and Classification of Target Variables in Structured Datasets
domain: tabular prediction (classification and regression)
editor_models: Claude Opus 5; Claude Sonnet 5; Claude Haiku 4.5; Grok 4.7; Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B (4-bit); Qwen3-4B (4-bit); Ministral-8B (4-bit)
headline: Claude Opus 5, shown a small table in context and writing every weight of a frozen network with no code execution or evaluation, matched closed-form optima on linear rungs and reached the irreducible error on three nonlinear rungs (e.g. 1.0000 on the parity rung vs 0.9662 for the same gradient-trained architecture), but failed on two oblique rungs (0.5084 on r2_kink, 0.5750 on s5_spiral).

title: Weight-space programming and mechanistic interpretability for model editing in particle physics
authors: Raphaël Bonnet-Guerrini; Johann Ioannou-Nikolaides; Troels Petersen
domain: particle physics (jet tagging foundation model, infrared safety)
headline: On the small OmniLearned model, the selected Claude Opus 5.5 WSP edit (no gradients, at most 50 queries) restored W efficiency after a soft photon from 54% to 79% with remaining response 0.05, matching LoRA fine-tuning (0.06, 79%) while changing about 10,000 versus 63,240 parameters and keeping physical response at 1.01 versus 0.90.

title: Writing Weights or Training Them? Spatial Reasoning through Weight-Space Programming and Low-Rank Adaptation
authors: Yalin Yang; Xiao Huang; Yanan Wu; Hao Yang; Ryan Zhenqi Zhou
domain: spatial reasoning (text)
editor_models: none for the main patch (uses MIT's published p50c, made with GPT-6 Astra); GPT-6 Astra (one further editing session)
headline: With thinking on, MIT's p50c patch raised Qwen3.5-0.8B from 0.0% to 22.1% (reference frame) and 19.2% to 33.7% (StepGame), while a rank-1 LoRA (0.09% trainable parameters) trained on worked solutions reached 100% and 98.8%; but the LoRA adapters collapsed off-target distance tasks from 94%/92% under p50c to 0-2%.

title: TrojanMaxxing: One-shotting VLM Backdoors with Weight-Space Programming
authors: Ahaan Dabholkar; Harshvardhan Patel; Michalis Polychronakis; Saurabh Bagchi
domain: security (visual backdoors in vision-language models: content moderation, OCR)
editor_models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code, xhigh effort); Claude Mythos 5.2 (Claude Code, xhigh effort)
headline: Frontier LLM agents, without gradients, implanted visually triggered backdoors in five VLMs with 93-100% attack success on content moderation and 78-100% on OCR while clean performance stayed within 0.02 of baseline, editing 0.0003-0.023% of weights for $9-30 per model.

title: Autonomous Parameter Surgery: How LLMs Implant Selective Backdoors into Language Models
authors: Xuyang Liu; Zhiwei Xu; Zirui Li; Jiabao Gao; Xiaolin Peng; Weixian Deng; Tian Qiu; Hai Wan; Xibin Zhao
domain: security (backdoor implantation in LLM sentiment classification)
headline: Over 18 sessions an inexpensive LLM editor, without gradients or layer hints, implanted a trigger backdoor with 99.2% mean in-domain attack success and 97.6% transfer to an unseen domain, keeping general capabilities within 1.7 points, at about $1.74 and 16.5 minutes per run.

title: SGNE-CC v2: Editing 205 Weight Columns in DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B Improves Greedy Accuracy and Reduces Unfinished Responses
domain: math reasoning, code generation, science QA and logic (reasoning-trace termination)
headline: A hand-derived norm-preserving rotation of 205 mlp.down_proj columns (0.0177% of weights) raised pooled greedy accuracy from 638 to 733 of 1,054 problems (+9.0 pp) but gave no significant gain under T = 0.6 sampling (72.3% to 73.3%, p = 0.4472).

title: Knowing Is Not Committing: Replicating MIT's weight-space edit and programming a truth-gated reflex into a 0.8B reasoning model (report)
domain: math reasoning
headline: On the same 40 MATH-500 problems MIT's released edit scores 55% with vLLM-style sampling but 25% with llama.cpp default sampling, and a loop direction built without any search agent lifts the unedited model from 10% to 37.5%.

title: SCALPELLO-GDP: a frontier model edits the weights of Qwen3.5-0.8B directly. One Householder reflection of a 'repetitive re-checking' direction lifts held-out math accuracy from 9.4% to 53.6% (384 paired problems), with no training
domain: math reasoning
headline: A Householder reflection of 12 attention output projections along an Astra-chosen 'repetitive re-checking' direction raised accuracy on 384 held-out practice problems from 9.38% to 53.65% at an 8,192-token cap, while a random-direction reflection gave +3.1 points on the development set.
